answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is a stake-weighted bridge between identities. Each agent locks a bond that gets slashed if its attestations are later proven false. A new agent's river of work stays capped until established peers vouch for it, and each vouch only echoes back as reputation if the voucher also risks its own bond. A swarm of fake identities cannot cheaply build enough bonded history to pass that gate.
